acceptance_criteria: AC-1: read docs/design/PRODUCT_CONTROL_PLANE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10 (pcp_storage_engine decision), docs/design/OPERATOR_CONSOLE_ARCHITECTURE.md, console/app.py and console/runner.py, and utils/collection_executor.py's workflow_argv to establish, as fact from the code, exactly which parts of today's console path are static-export-shaped (HTML/JSON snapshot formatting) versus which parts already produce structured, DB-ready data (the D1-D7 producers, registry, resolver). This is the evidentiary basis for the whole document -- do not assume the extent of the mismatch, show it.

AC-2: produce docs/design/UI2_0_ARCHITECTURE_REQUIREMENTS.md (status DRAFT), following the same document shape as docs/design/PRIVATE_REPLAY_ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/design/M14_LOCAL_LDAP_AUTHORIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md, that captures the Product Owner's 11-point functional target verbatim-referenced and organized as: (1) empty-shell UI, (2) DB-backed state + LDAP auth + role-based menu authorization (link to M14's D7 design, do not re-derive LDAP/AD decisions -- reference them), (3) device onboarding (discovery + manual, no static HTML generation, no unnecessary data pull), (4) auto config/inventory population post-onboarding eligible for compliance checking, (5) configuration-only fetch scripts that write straight to DB with no formatting side-output, (6) inventory-only fetch with no other data pulled, (7) compliance: operator selects benchmark (e.g. CIS) then applies to selected devices, (8) backup: add/select-device/schedule, plus drift comparison against prior backups, (9) failover menu auto-populated from live active/passive state at configurable intervals, (10) a live/dynamic project-plan view, optionally GitHub-sourced.

AC-3: for each of the 11 points, state as a concrete requirement: (a) what data/module already exists today that can feed it (name the real file/function), (b) what is genuinely new work, (c) whether it depends on the DB-engine decision, the M14 LDAP design, or is independent of both.

AC-4: resolve, as real recommendations with stated tradeoffs (not left open), these cross-cutting sub-decisions: (a) full ground-up rewrite (discard the static-export console entirely) versus an incremental DB + typed live-state API layer added over the existing D1-D7/resolver/registry foundation, reusing collection modules as data producers only -- state which better serves the Product Owner's own stated constraint that Line-1 (M-series) keeps shipping in parallel and maturing features 'evolve' into UI2.0 one at a time; (b) storage engine choice, resolving pcp_storage_engine's deferred criteria against UI2.0's live-query/role-based-access/audit needs specifically (not a generic re-derivation -- build on section 10's existing criteria); (c) deployment runtime split -- must every request-serving/UI component be one language, or can collection modules stay Python subprocesses/workers behind a typed boundary while a new service layer is written in another language; (d) the Product Owner's explicit ask: whether and how much of this should be written in Java instead of Python, given a stated corporate-infrastructure requirement for Java. Evaluate at minimum: (i) Java only for the new UI2.0 service/API/DB-access layer, with existing Python collection modules kept as-is and invoked as subprocess workers or via a queue/API boundary (polyglot, minimal rewrite of already-frozen/tested collection logic); (ii) full Python-to-Java rewrite of the collection modules themselves; state the cost, risk, and rework-of-frozen-work implications of each, and give a clear recommendation with reasoning, but do not treat this as decided -- it is a requirements-document recommendation only.

AC-5: explicitly state what this document does NOT decide: final storage engine, final language/runtime split, final LDAP persistence model (defer entirely to the M14 draft), and that no implementation movement is authorized by this document alone. Also explicitly reconcile with the Product Owner's stated intent that this evolves incrementally alongside Line-1 rather than as a stop-the-world replacement -- describe what an incremental migration path could look like (e.g. UI2.0 shell + DB + auth first, wired to read-only views of existing evidence store, expanding module-by-module) as one section, not as the decided plan.

AC-6: no implementation, no test changes, no project-state file changes beyond adding this document and a short project/backlog.json note pointing to it -- same validation floor as prior design-only movements (git diff --check, privacy gate, no code/test touched).

baseline.authority: No existing frozen contract targets this scope. docs/design/PRODUCT_CONTROL_PLANE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10 already records the open pcp_storage_engine decision (filesystem-first evidence store, Postgres opt-in path exists for scheduler/job/CAS-metadata state only, engine choice deferred) -- this document extends that same open decision, it does not reopen or contradict it.

Product Owner explicitly wants the current M-series (Line 1) to keep shipping in parallel; this document must describe an incremental evolution path where maturing Line-1 features (D1-D7 producers, registry, resolver) become UI2.0's live data sources one at a time, not a stop-the-world rewrite.

entries.subject: UI2.0 requirements draft merged (PR #140) -- resolved sub-questions and the still-open scope choice
entries.text: docs/design/UI2_0_ARCHITECTURE_REQUIREMENTS.md (DRAFT) merged via PR #140, merge commit d519581. AUDIT (section 2): the static-export coupling is six run_html_export tail calls in application/workflows/* (checkpoint.py:195/312/536/703/724, maintenance.py:297, preflight.py:183) plus the eight *_ui.py payload builders as the console's only read model (C1-4 parity); the registry, M4 SQLite store, seven Postgres-capable evidence concerns, the Postgres-capable admission coordinator and the pure D4/M10.2 resolver chain are already DB-ready. One notable finding: build_compliance_posture takes the configuration UI projection as its subject input. RESOLVED AS RECOMMENDATIONS (section 6): X-1 incremental DB + typed live-state API over the existing foundation, not a rewrite -- the only option compatible with Line-1 shipping in parallel; X-2 PostgreSQL as production engine against PCP section 10's own criteria, SQLite stays local, CAS/recovery blobs stay on the volume; X-3 collection modules stay Python workers behind a queue-through-database boundary (argv template stays in workflow_argv only); X-4 Java, if the corporate requirement is binding on services, only for the new service/API/DB layer (option i); a Python-to-Java collector rewrite (option ii) is recommended against because it resets every REAL_ENV_VALIDATED collector to PLANNED and halts Line-1. STILL OPEN (section 8): the rewrite-vs-incremental scope decision itself, the engine, the language split, the LDAP persistence model (deferred to M14). NEEDS PO DECISION BEFORE ANY FREEZE (section 9): C-1 CON.0 payload parity + bundler rule vs a separate shell; C-2 'role-based menu authorization' as menu hiding contradicts frozen AC-CS-33; C-3 backup add/select/schedule from a browser vs class 1 console refusal and the C-D7 gate; C-4 multi-user browser login is the DEPLOY.1A shape, not M14's single-operator TTY bind; plus U-1, the exact content of the Java requirement. Recommended next: a PO DECIDE episode (Sonnet 5, extended high), not an engineering movement. Validation: full parallel regression 3022 passed / 25 skipped / 2 failed (the two pre-existing DLP-token collision tests, same as PR #138, findings in files this PR does not touch); git diff --check clean; privacy gate vs origin/main baseline PASS 0 new findings. CI validate job was still pending at self-merge time; local evidence is the merge basis.
